text: The numbers are proven correct. Now a real performance problem: the VP reports an eight-to-ten-second delay just clicking into a single store. We diagnose the actual cause in the model, not the visuals.

Performance Analyzer isolates it immediately: almost the entire delay is DAX query time, not rendering. DAX Studio narrows it further -- nearly all of that time sits in the formula engine, the classic signature of row-by-row evaluation instead of a set-based query.

The culprit is one measure, Total Units Sold, written with SUMX wrapped around FILTER of ALL of fact_sales -- manually re-filtering row by row instead of letting the model's existing relationships do the work.

Rewritten as a plain CALCULATE of SUM, it lets the dimension-to-fact relationship do the filtering automatically -- the same query drops from roughly seven point eight seconds to about two hundred and forty milliseconds.
Every other measure in the model already used CALCULATE correctly -- only this one, added later, had the anti-pattern, which is exactly why auditing the whole model after a fix matters.
Thirty times faster, with zero changes to the visual itself. Next: the first real numbers, and what the business actually learns from them.
